test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Mechanic) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: For a given subcooling in °C, the increase in refrigeration effect is ____________.

options.text: proportional to the specific heat of the liquid
proportional to the entropy of the liquid
proportional to the irreversibility of the liquid
inversely proportional to the specific heat of the liquid

solution:
The correct answer is __proportional to the specific heat of the liquid****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Subcooling__ is the process of lowering the temperature of a liquid below its saturation temperature.
 
• The refrigeration effect increases as the liquid is subcooled further.
 
• The increase in refrigeration effect is directly proportional to the specific heat of the liquid being used in the system.
 
• Specific heat indicates the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of the liquid by one degree Celsius.
 
• Subcooling ensures better efficiency of the refrigeration cycle and prevents compressor damage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Specific Heat:**
 
 
• Specific heat is a property of substances that determines how much heat they can absorb or release during a temperature change.
 
• Higher specific heat values lead to a greater refrigeration effect during subcooling.
 
 
 
• **Entropy:**
 
 
• Entropy is a measure of disorder or randomness in a system.
 
• While entropy is essential in thermodynamics, it does not directly affect refrigeration effect during subcooling.
 
 
 
• **Irreversibility:**
 
 
• Irreversibility refers to energy losses due to factors like friction, heat transfer, and other inefficiencies.
 
• Minimizing irreversibility improves system performance but is not proportional to refrigeration effect.
